correctness.rationale: The median projection identity is exact. Adjacent-low pair intervals remain disjoint forever. For opposite-low pairs at gamma<=1/2, both within-pair widths shrink by 1-gamma, the interpair gap by 1-2gamma, and the two interface opinions have conserved sum; all four converge to the middle-order-statistic midpoint. Of six equiprobable low-pair positions exactly two are opposite. For any gamma>1/2 explicit strict inequalities make a separated adjacent-low arrangement in one step from an open opposite-low region, proving strict probability loss. Finite rational and numerical checker is supplemental, not the basis of the theorem.

value.rationale: The source expressly distinguishes universal consensus from consensus for individual starts and reports numerical frequency depending on heterogeneous settings. The exact 1/3 law and its sharp gamma=1/2 failure quantify a concrete nontrivial initial-condition basin, expose aggressive-update-induced polarization without any topology or influence change, and give a closed-form consensus selection rule; these are a motivated complete sharp phase boundary rather than an arbitrary parameter-slice computation. The three-cycle always converges to its initial median for every 0<gamma<1, proving that the four-cycle is the smallest simple ring displaying this dependence.
